evidence.design: Randomized single-blind crossover; 14 healthy young men; equal-energy meals, 45% energy from fat; 13-hour indirect calorimetry
evidence.result: Oleate shortened time to peak RQ; oleate and ALA shortened time to food quotient versus palmitate. Acylcarnitine associations do not directly measure shuttle flux.
evidence.retrieval: Primary indexed abstract; publisher full-text request returned 403. Exact meal recipes and food delivery were not retrieved.

evidence.result: Earlier formula-diet experiment found chronic, not acute, palmitate/oleate differences. Distinct exposure and endpoints; not replication of the 2026 time-based switching result.

recommendation: Retain positive mechanism-specific research candidate. Retrieve full recipes, fatty-acid composition, carbohydrate/protein matching and preparation before implementing a reproducible SOP. Do not infer equivalent effects of fish, nuts, olive oil or ALA foods.

evidence.design: Small open-label study; five mitochondrial-myopathy patients with matched controls; niacin escalated to 750–1000 mg/day; patients 10 months, controls 4 months
evidence.result: NAD repletion and muscle mitochondrial biogenesis reported. Not an ordinary-food exposure or placebo-controlled estimate of general efficacy.
evidence.retrieval: Primary indexed abstract and author-hosted manuscript search excerpts; primary trial registration NCT03973203.

recommendation: Promising formulation-specific research protocol. Hold general PM9 dietary admission: high-dose nicotinic acid is not total dietary B3, nicotinamide or protein, and response in NAD-deficient myopathy cannot establish food-level biogenesis or ADHD benefit. A supported complete conversion/active-target record and exposure assessment are needed.

evidence.design: Five-month NR escalation to 1 g/day; 20 BMI-discordant twin pairs enrolled, 16 analysed; four concordant pairs provided a small placebo comparison. Mitochondrial imaging/omics were performed in the treated discordant cohort, not a powered placebo comparison.
evidence.result: Type-I-fibre mitochondrial number and area increased; respiration not measured. Authors explicitly leave benefit, mechanism and possible compensatory response unresolved.

evidence.design: Randomized placebo-controlled 12 weeks, 40 obese insulin-resistant men; 1 g NR twice daily
evidence.result: No effect on muscle mitochondrial respiration, associated proteins, fractional area or morphology. Not evidence that the five-month result is impossible; duration/population differ.

evidence.design: Randomized placebo-controlled crossover, 12 older men; 1 g/day for 21 days
evidence.result: Muscle NAD metabolome changed without improved mitochondrial bioenergetics. Exposure/biochemical engagement alone does not establish biogenesis.

recommendation: Hold admission and keep positive and null studies together. Resolve NR stereochemical/form identity, complete conversion tracing, and define a formulation/population-specific proposition before any new dietary admission. No ordinary-food mapping fabricated.
